description: Agent GovCon: submit a deliverable or progress report with the contract’s deliverable schedule and the acceptance records: the report with its reference, the contract number it cites and each deliverable it claims with its id, the deliverable, the due date it states, the day delivered, its status (accepted, submitted, pending or rejected) and who it says accepted it; the schedule with its contract number, each deliverable it requires with its due date, and each party the contract names to accept deliverables; the acceptance records with each deliverable accepted, the day and who signed. The signed report gives the report and the schedule, each claimed deliverable paired with the schedule both ways, each due date read against the schedule’s and each delivery against its due date, each deliverable marked accepted read against the acceptance records, and each acceptance read against the parties the contract names, and counts them, and names a divergent report: a deliverable the report claims that the schedule never required, a due date unlike the schedule, a deliverable marked accepted with no acceptance record, and acceptance signed by a party the contract does not name; then a scheduled deliverable left out, a late delivery and another contract number, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No claimed or scheduled deliverables, no due date on both sides, no statuses, or no named acceptors where acceptances are signed leaves those points unverified. Deliverables read by their words with plurals folded, dates by the day, and acceptors as parties without case, punctuation or a legal suffix. This reads the report against the schedule and the acceptance records as stated. Verdict govcon_deliverable_divergent, govcon_deliverable_partial, govcon_deliverable_unverified or govcon_deliverable_consistent. POST /api/govcon-deliverable-check. Reads the government contracting records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between contracting documents only: it never submits a bid or proposal, never registers or certifies a vendor in any government system, never contacts an agency and never decides eligibility or award, which stay with the contracting agency, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent GovCon reads government contracting records across the procurement lifecycle for consistency between the documents and the terms they answer to: a solicitation, a vendor’s eligibility record, a proposal or bid, a price proposal or pricing volume, an award notice, a contract modification, a deliverable or progress report and an invoice or payment voucher, each against its own sections and the notice it follows, the solicitation’s set-aside, eligibility, submission and pricing terms, the winning price and eligibility record, the base award and prior modifications, the deliverable schedule, or the payment terms and acceptance record it should agree with. The family reads procurement, the government buying goods and services under contract terms, and reads the records against each other. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-govcon-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-govcon/.
